accounting.rationale: Original PDF125 lines33-34 defines the nonallocatable nonpointer dummy-array category and its effective-argument shape. The actual extent/bound effect is accounted under p4, not a separate no-op definition program.
An ALLOCATABLE dummy declared with colons has a different category; a valid deferred-shape declaration is not an invalid assumed-shape declaration merely because its spelling is similar.
Array pointers use their own association and deferred-shape rules. Do not transfer ordinary dummy lower-bound defaults to a pointer dummy.
PENDING complete dummy/actual and explicit-interface source context under15.4.2.2 and15.5.2.5, not an ordinary local colon declaration.
The array category requires nonzero rank. Scalar entities reached through a zero-size bound vector or RANK(0) retain their actual category and inquiry restrictions.
Shape derives from the effective argument, not necessarily its lower bounds. The runtime p4 requirement retains the complete association premises; no copying or ABI mechanism is promised.
PDF125 line35 has a required colon and optional scalar lower-bound, whose canonical specification-expression definition remains R816.
PDF125 line36 is one explicit-bounds-expr followed by a colon, not a list that mixes a vector with additional scalar shape entries.
PDF126 lines1-3 gives guarded rank determination followed by scalar/array classification. The latter is not an extra executable classifier.
Nonzero established rank gives an assumed-shape array. Total size can still be zero.
A bound vector of size zero establishes a scalar, unlike a rank-one vector containing a zero lower bound. Do not impose array-only inquiry arguments on the scalar.
PDF126 lines4-5 retains the vector, otherwise scalar, otherwise one alternatives and their dimension scope.
PDF126 lines6-8 specifies corresponding extents and the upper-bound relation. UBOUND/LBOUND have additional whole-array and empty-dimension result rules.

requirements.title: A scalar assumed-shape specification has an optional lower bound and a colon
requirements.definition: The scalar assumed-shape-spec is a colon with an optional preceding lower-bound. R816 defines that bound as a scalar integer specification expression. The list form and the R821 bound-vector form are different R814 alternatives, and the entity's attributes and role determine whether a colon declaration is assumed shape or deferred shape.

Exclude valid R821 vector parses and R814 explicit/deferred/assumed-size alternatives before assigning a grammar error. Keep one canonical owner rather than duplicate lower-bound negatives.

requirements.title: A vector assumed-shape specification is a bound expression followed by a colon
requirements.definition: The assumed-shape-bounds-spec has one explicit-bounds-expr followed by a colon. R819/C833 give its integer, restricted-expression, rank-one and constant-size premises. Its values need not be constant and its size can be zero. It is not a component-array-spec alternative under R740.

pending.vector-lower-bounds: PENDING an ordinary INTEGER dummy x(lower:) in a complete explicit interface, with a prior fixed-size rank-one INTEGER lower vector and a same-rank actual. Use a two-element constant vector and a restricted dummy vector whose values vary across separate valid calls, without changing expected values from an affected descriptor.
pending.zero-size-vector-boundary: PENDING a prior rank-one INTEGER constant vector of size0 and the resulting scalar dummy, supplied with a defined scalar actual through an explicit interface. A vector containing one zero element instead specifies rank1 with lower bound0. No array-only inquiry on the ordinary scalar.
pending.bound-expression-contract: PENDING exact canonical R819/C833 rank/type/restricted/constant-size negative-and-repair relations and R814 alternative parsing. Do not mix one vector-bounds-spec with additional scalar list entries, expand R740 component grammar, or duplicate the canonical expression cases. These F2023 forms are not optional capability skips.

requirements.title: Without a RANK clause, list length or bound-vector size establishes rank
requirements.source: 8.5.8.3 p2 rank-determination clauses, physical PDF126, lines1-3
requirements.definition: When a rank-clause does not specify rank, the rank comes from the number of colons in the assumed-shape-spec-list or the size of the vector in assumed-shape-bounds-spec. The vector-size route can establish rank zero. Zero total array size does not reduce a nonzero established rank.

requirements.title: Assumed-shape lower bounds come from the vector, scalar specifications or default one
requirements.definition: A present explicit-bounds-expr supplies lower bounds for every dimension. Otherwise each specified scalar lower-bound supplies its dimension's bound, with one for an omitted lower bound. These are dummy bounds, not an unconditional copy of effective-argument lower bounds. Inquiry normalization remains separate from the declared values.

pending.vector-ordinal-lowers: PENDING dummy x(lower:) with the two-element vector values[-5,7], including a vector declared with a different index origin. Expect lower[-5,7], upper[-3,8], shape[3,2]. Use ordinal element-to-dimension correspondence and independent literal results.

Batch314 assumed-shape lower-bound effects: two run/effect/f2023 programs observe assumed-shape dummy lower bounds. The nonempty program passes a defined actual of shape [3,2] with nonunit actual lower bounds to dummies `x(:,:)`, `x(0:,-3:)` and `x(0:,:)`, requiring literal lower and upper bounds for omitted, specified and mixed scalar lower specifications. The empty-inquiry program passes `empty(5:3,-2:1)` to `x(5:,-2:)` and requires the legal whole-dummy empty-dimension LBOUND=[1,-2] and UBOUND=[0,1] without element access. Feature mutations alter the dummy lower specifications or change the empty actual to a singleton first dimension, so each assertion is load-bearing.
requirements.oracle_limitation:
Whole arrays differ from expressions/sections under9.5.2 and the inquiry rules. Overall zero size does not normalize every dimension. Pointer/allocatable dummies are not this category, and scalar zero-vector entities cannot be fed to ordinary array-only inquiries.

Batch314 assumed-shape lower-bound effects boundaries: Only scalar-list lower-bound effects and the empty whole-dummy inquiry boundary are covered. Vector lower-bound forms remain pending because the reference compiler rejects `x(lower:)` vector-bound syntax here.

requirements.title: Effective-argument extents and the dummy lower bound determine the upper bound
requirements.definition: Each dimension of an assumed-shape dummy has the extent of the corresponding effective-argument dimension. With dummy lower bound d and effective extent s, the upper bound is s+d-1. This does not promise actual/dummy address identity, a copying mechanism or unconditional equality between the declared upper bound and UBOUND's normalized empty-dimension result.
